args.body:
Hi Dora! I just took a look at your personal website at www.dora-website.com and wanted to share some feedback.

What works well:
- It's clean and straightforward — you get straight to the point about who the site belongs to, with your contact email (dora@gmail.com) easy to find. For a personal site, that simplicity is a real strength; it loads fast and doesn't distract visitors.

Suggestions to make it stronger:
- Add a short intro or "About Me" section — a couple of sentences about who you are, what you do, or what you're interested in would give visitors an immediate sense of your personality and make the site feel more welcoming.
- Consider adding some content beyond the email: recent projects, a résumé/CV, photos, or links to your other profiles (GitHub, LinkedIn, etc.). Right now there's very little to browse.
- A bit of visual design would help too — even a simple layout with a heading, some sections, and a footer can make a minimal site look intentional rather than unfinished.
- If you do keep it minimal, adding a small navigation menu or anchors (About / Contact) would make it easier to move around.

Overall, it's a nice, no-fluff starting point — just a little more substance and polish would take it from a placeholder to a site that really represents you. Nice work getting it live!

Best,
Emma Johnson

Hi Eve! I had a look at your blog at www.eve-blog.com and wanted to send along some feedback.

What works well:
- The site has a clear identity right away — it's your blog, and you immediately share a personal detail (that hiking is your favorite hobby). That personal touch is exactly what makes a blog feel like it belongs to a real person rather than a generic template.
- It's pleasantly simple and easy to read.

Suggestions to make it stronger:
- Since hiking is your passion, that's a great thread to build on — consider a few actual blog posts about your hikes: trail write-ups, gear notes, photos, or a "best trails near me" list. Right now there's a great hook but no content to follow it.
- Add an "About Me" section with a bit more background, and maybe a short list of recent posts or archives so visitors can find something to read.
- A small navigation menu (Home / About / Posts / Contact) and a footer with your email or social links would make the blog easier to navigate and give readers a way to follow along.
- Some visual polish — a header image, consistent post formatting, and tags for your entries — would make it feel more like a finished blog.

Overall, it's a friendly and authentic start, and the hiking theme gives you a great niche to own. A few real posts and some structure would make it shine. Keep it up!

Best,
Emma Johnson
